narrative.summary: The BIS and the committees it hosts have so far addressed AI mainly through reports rather than standards. A group of central banks working through the BIS Americas Office set out an AI governance framework with ten practical actions for central banks (2025), and the BIS reported to G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors on authorities' use of AI for policy purposes (2025). The Basel Committee has discussed AI at its meetings and published an informational newsletter on AI and machine learning (2022), but has not issued AI-specific supervisory standards.

instruments.summary: Report by a task force of central banks (Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, United States) with the BIS on how central banks can govern their own use of AI. It identifies risks such as data security and confidentiality, model errors including hallucinations, and reputational harm, and proposes an adaptive governance framework building on the three lines of defence, with ten practical actions: an AI committee, responsible-use principles, an AI framework, an inventory and mapping of AI tools, risk and control assessment, monitoring, incident reporting, skills, and periodic review.
instruments.current_status: Published by the BIS on 29 January 2025 as a report of the Consultative Group on Risk Management. Not binding; offered as practical guidance for central banks.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 29 January 2025 from BIS page; PDF cover printed 'January 2025'. No author-views disclaimer found in PDF front matter. Issued by a group of member central banks; included as guidance because it proposes a governance framework, not only analysis.

instruments.official_title: The use of artificial intelligence for policy purposes
instruments.english_title: The use of artificial intelligence for policy purposes
instruments.summary: Report on how central banks, financial regulators and supervisors use AI in their policy work, from big data and machine learning to large language models. It sets out practical use cases and identifies the conditions for responsible adoption, notably data governance, investment in staff skills and IT infrastructure, and cooperation among authorities.
instruments.current_status: BIS report published on 10 October 2025 and submitted to the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors ahead of their October 2025 meeting.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date and 'prepared for G20 FMCBG' from BIS page othp100. Included under the brief's rule for reports delivered to the G20; borderline (analytical). Drop if the site keeps only guidance texts. | Independent check 2026-10-21: source does not say 'Not binding'

membership_note: BIS members are 63 central banks and monetary authorities, not governments; the list shows the 61 countries whose central banks are members (the European Central Bank and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority are also members). The Basel Committee and other BIS-hosted committees have their own, smaller memberships of central banks and supervisors.
